title: Completed-packet archival is not bound to the validated packet identity or bytes
observed_behavior: The preview validates a packet and stores only its ID and source/target paths. Apply checks only that targets remain absent, then moves whatever bytes are currently at each source. An explicitly requested filename whose JSON id differs is also skipped before packet validation and produces an empty, non-refused plan.
expected_invariant: Archival must move only the exact, still-complete packet identity and content that passed validation, and every explicitly selected malformed or identity-mismatched packet must fail closed with an actionable refusal.
root_cause: ArchiveMove carries no validated source hash, status, completion date, or filename-to-payload identity proof for apply-time comparison; requested selection switches from filename stem to payload id before validation.
failure_scenario: A packet is edited by another process after plan construction, or its filename and payload id diverge. The command can archive planned/in-progress or otherwise changed evidence, or report a successful no-op for an invalid explicitly requested packet.
evidence: Current archive_completed.py SHA-256 cf13c75e47d142a2d667f790d238a5764c53d23eb87e93a9021e3c8d5752bb5e validates at lines 114-178, but apply_plan lines 201-223 never reloads or hashes a source.

Temporary-root reproduction built a one-move, zero-refusal plan from a valid complete packet, rewrote that source to status=planned with date_completed=null, and apply_plan moved it; the source disappeared and the archived payload retained status=planned.

A second temporary-root reproduction stored payload id MP-CHANGE-2026-0602-903 in the explicitly requested MP-CHANGE-2026-0602-902.json; build_plan returned zero moves, zero refusals, zero invalid entries, and zero already-archived entries.

The focused tests cover selection, active refusal, existing target refusal, normal apply/idempotence, and generator-failure rollback, but no source mutation or filename/payload-id mismatch between selection and mutation.
existing_safeguards: Plan construction validates complete status, date_completed, packet schema, and target absence; apply snapshots generated outputs and rolls back ordinary exceptions.
safeguard_gap: Those safeguards are time-of-check only. No optimistic content check binds apply to the validated bytes, and explicit selector identity mismatches bypass validation rather than becoming refusals.
recommended_remediation: Include the validated source SHA-256 and normalized packet identity/status/date in each plan move. Immediately before any mutation, reload every source, require filename/id agreement, revalidate all packets, and compare hashes as one preflight; refuse the whole tranche on any drift. Add an explicit mismatch diagnostic before requested filtering.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: stricter optimistic checks can reject concurrently edited packets, which is the intended safe behavior; rollback/interruption changes need Windows filesystem validation.
validation_rung: Focused change-control unit tests with mutation and identity-mismatch injection, then canonical change-packet validation and archive preview/apply tests in a temporary repository; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current change-control root cause; no existing worker finding mentions archive_completed plan identity, build/apply drift, or explicit selector mismatch.

title: Assertion inventory silently excludes custom PowerShell assertions and inline failure checks
observed_behavior: The claimed exact assertion-line census recognizes only Assert-True, Invoke-PowerShellBehaviorCheck, Python assert, and raise AssertionError at line starts. The current legacy regression script also contains a custom Assert-TV helper with 18 invocation lines and 582 inline if (...) { throw ... } failure lines; none enters the coverage set, yet the canonical inventory validates with zero findings.
expected_invariant: A machine-readable inventory advertised as covering every assertion-bearing line exactly once must discover all assertion constructs used by the governed script, including custom assertion helpers and embedded inline failure checks, or explicitly classify them as exclusions.
root_cause: Coverage is defined by a fixed four-regex allowlist rather than PowerShell/embedded-language syntax or a declared, validated assertion-helper registry. The exact-once loop can therefore prove completeness only over its own incomplete detector output.
failure_scenario: A unique legacy behavior is expressed only through Assert-TV or an inline throw, then its surrounding mapping is removed or misclassified. The strict checker remains green because the assertion never existed in its coverage universe, allowing preservation/removal decisions to rely on an incomplete inventory.
evidence: Current checker SHA-256 b7b5e20c18d07f3fd0daade80df3d5bac48dab12f74ec82606fb5288eb8f2f38 defines exactly four patterns at lines 132-149 and builds all coverage from their results at lines 799-857.
Current canonical validation returned validator_findings=0 and detected_assertion_lines=528.

A read-only census of the governed legacy script found 18 Assert-TV call lines (3407-3424), recognized=0, and 582 inline if/throw lines, recognized=0. Assert-TV itself throws on five TV parsing mismatches.
Current tests exercise uncovered/multiply-covered behavior and exclusions only for the same four recognized syntaxes; they include no custom PowerShell assertion helper or inline throw fixture.
existing_safeguards: Active spans must be unique/non-overlapping, recognized assertion lines need exactly one owner, and exclusions need unique recognized anchors with reasons.
safeguard_gap: All exact-once safeguards operate after incomplete assertion discovery, so a missed construct is indistinguishable from a non-assertion line.
tests_missing: a differential census against the current governed script
recommended_remediation: Parse the PowerShell AST and embedded script bodies where feasible, or maintain an explicit schema-backed assertion-helper registry that includes Assert-TV and inline conditional throws. Fail when previously unseen Assert-* calls or test-like throw constructs appear, and add current-script census fixtures proving the coverage universe before exact-once ownership.
remediation_risk: Medium: broad throw detection can include harness/control-flow errors, so the detector needs typed classifications and explicit exclusions rather than counting every throw blindly.
validation_rung: Focused checker tests for custom helpers and inline throws, canonical --json inventory validation, and a reviewed current-script assertion census; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from AUDIT-FIND-W11-021: that finding loses unreadable reference evidence in another removal checker, while this root cause omits assertion lines before inventory coverage begins.

title: Removal gate trusts nonexistent replacement paths and free-form success prose
observed_behavior: A removed unique/covered block is accepted when equivalent_coverage merely contains nonempty paths/evidence and any validation string contains a positive token. Paths are never resolved or checked, and negated text such as 'replacement did not pass' is classified as passing.
expected_invariant: Removal of unique legacy coverage must require existing, repository-contained replacement paths and structured, unambiguously successful validation evidence tied to those replacements.
root_cause: The gate applies truthiness checks to equivalent coverage and tokenizes arbitrary prose for pass words instead of validating typed path and result records.
failure_scenario: An inventory author mistypes or later deletes the replacement test, or records a failed command in prose containing the word pass. The checker clears TSI028 and authorizes removal even though no executable replacement proof exists.
evidence: Current _validation_passed returned True for ['replacement did not pass'].
Current test_replacement.py does not exist, but the focused unit test inserts that path plus 'passed: python -m unittest ...' and expects validate_inventory(...)=[]; the test passes.
The current canonical inventory has ten removed blocks and presently no missing equivalent paths, so this is a fail-open gate defect rather than a claim that current replacements are absent.
All-worker structured deduplication found no existing equivalent_coverage, validation_passed, or subsystem-inventory finding.
existing_safeguards: Removed unique/covered blocks require nonempty equivalent_coverage fields and some validation item containing a recognized positive word; unclear_preserve blocks cannot be removed.
safeguard_gap: Neither replacement existence/currentness nor result provenance and negation are validated.
tests_present: nonempty free-form replacement evidence is accepted
tests_missing: structured command exit code and selector-to-path correlation
recommended_remediation: Define typed equivalent-coverage entries with normalized repository paths, require each current path to exist and be an eligible test/check, and replace prose token matching with structured validation records containing command, exit_code, result, timestamp/evidence hash, and exact covered path IDs. Reject ambiguous prose in strict mode.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: existing historical evidence may need migration to the typed shape, and strict validation may expose stale removal records.
validation_rung: Focused schema/checker tests for path existence, containment, negation, and structured exit results, followed by canonical inventory validation; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New fail-open mechanism in the subsystem inventory. It is related to but distinct from AUDIT-FIND-W11-021, which swallows read errors in a different legacy-removal checker.

title: Malformed top-level inventory bypasses structured validation and crashes JSON mode
observed_behavior: load_inventory accepts any JSON value, but main calls inventory.get('legacy_script') before validate_inventory invokes _validate_top_level. A syntactically valid top-level JSON array therefore raises uncaught AttributeError even under --json.
expected_invariant: Every malformed inventory, including a valid JSON value of the wrong top-level type, must return the checker's documented nonzero status and structured TSI finding payload in JSON mode.
root_cause: Legacy-script path resolution dereferences the unvalidated payload before the top-level type guard.
failure_scenario: During an inventory edit or automated generation, the file becomes [] or another non-object JSON value. CI and callers expecting parseable --json diagnostics receive a Python traceback instead, breaking deterministic evidence collection and obscuring TSI validation details.
evidence: Current main lines 888-896 handles I/O/JSON syntax errors, then line 900 calls inventory.get before validate_inventory at line 912.
Temporary-file reproduction invoked main(['--inventory', <file containing []>, '--json']) and caught uncaught AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'.
_validate_top_level already has the correct object-type finding path, but execution never reaches it in this case.
Current focused tests do not invoke main with a wrong-type top-level JSON value.
existing_safeguards: JSON syntax, file I/O, and later schema/type errors are converted to findings; main returns 1 when validate_inventory reports them.
safeguard_gap: The first top-level dereference occurs outside and before those safeguards.
tests_present: CLI success behavior through canonical checks
tests_missing: CLI wrong-top-level-type cases in text and JSON modes
recommended_remediation: Validate the loaded value immediately, or resolve legacy_script only after a successful top-level object check. Route every load/type/decode failure through one structured TSI000/TSI002 result and add subprocess-level JSON parsing assertions.
remediation_risk: Low: reordering validation changes only malformed-input diagnostics and exit behavior.
validation_rung: Focused direct and subprocess CLI tests for object, array, scalar, decode, and missing-file inputs, plus canonical --json validation; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current CLI error-semantics defect; no current finding is located on this checker path.

title: Retrieval acceptance reports expected-test coverage when only unrelated tests are returned
observed_behavior: run_benchmark computes expected_test_hit for each fixture case but increments high_risk_test_hits from test_hit, which is true for any selected or related test. acceptance_findings labels that aggregate as expected-test coverage. It also computes required-layer completeness without any acceptance condition.
expected_invariant: The Release 1 check must fail whenever a high-risk case omits all fixture-declared expected tests, and fixture fields named required_layers must have an explicit enforced acceptance policy rather than silently informational treatment.
root_cause: The acceptance aggregate is wired to a generic evidence-category presence bit instead of the already-computed expected_test_hit, while acceptance thresholds omit the required-layer metric.
failure_scenario: Retrieval returns an irrelevant or merely adjacent test for every high-risk task and misses every declared expected test or required layer. The benchmark emits 100% high-risk test coverage, --check exits successfully, and release/change-packet evidence records a false green.
evidence: Current benchmark SHA-256 2069bd76c6a64b1eab2e5d8afcf250841cc8976ac5c02ca70cc11c120f6c1232 computes expected_test_hit at line 151 but increments from test_hit at line 160; acceptance line 221 calls the result expected-test coverage.

A patched 48-case run returned the authority, boundary, and one unrelated test for every high-risk case. All 48 case rows had expected_test_hit=False, reported high_risk_test_coverage was 1.0, and acceptance_findings returned [].

The canonical current 48-case run had 19 expected-test misses, including 8 of 29 high-risk cases (settings library/preset/template, queue snapshot/engine, and three media policy cases), yet reported high_risk_test_coverage=1.0, vertical_slice_completeness=0.5887, acceptance_findings=[], and --check exit 0.
A payload with vertical_slice_completeness=0.0 and every currently enforced threshold passing also returned no acceptance finding.
The completed retrieval change packet records PASS based on 100% high-risk test/boundary coverage, so the mislabeled aggregate feeds durable release evidence.
The only focused threshold test constructs aggregate metrics directly; it does not exercise per-case aggregation, expected_test_paths, or a required-layer failure.
existing_safeguards: Fixture paths must exist, case IDs are unique, repo_context failures raise, and authority/irrelevance/boundary/latency thresholds are enforced.
safeguard_gap: The exact expected-test obligation is computed only for display, and required-layer misses cannot fail acceptance.
tests_missing: end-to-end run_benchmark acceptance with a controlled service
recommended_remediation: Increment high_risk_test_hits from expected_test_hit and rename any generic test-presence metric separately. Define and document the required-layer threshold (prefer exact per-high-risk-case obligations), expose failing case IDs in acceptance output, and add controlled end-to-end aggregation tests.
remediation_risk: Low to medium: the corrected benchmark may newly fail current retrieval and require ranking/fixture adjustments; production media behavior is unaffected.
validation_rung: Focused benchmark unit tests with a fake service, canonical 48-case --check run, generated-context checks, and updated packet evidence if results change; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from AUDIT-FIND-W11-008, which truncates route records before retrieval; this finding shows the benchmark can certify missing fixture-declared tests even when its input index is complete.

title: Remediation changelog segmentation leaves a retry-blocking partial archive on write failure

locations.symbol: archive write and post-write tamper tests

observed_behavior: segment_archive creates the final archive directory, writes segment files, overwrites the authoritative changelog with its compact index, writes the manifest, and only then verifies. There is no temporary staging directory, atomic publish, source snapshot restoration, or failure cleanup; any later retry refuses because the archive directory already exists.
expected_invariant: Mechanical archival of preserved historical evidence must publish source, segments, and manifest as one recoverable transaction, leaving either the original ledger intact or a completely verified archive that the command can safely retry.
root_cause: The final paths are mutated sequentially before verification with no transaction/rollback boundary, while directory existence is treated as an unconditional retry blocker.
failure_scenario: A disk, sharing, interruption, encoding, or verification failure occurs after some writes. Operators are left with mixed source/archive generations and must manually infer recovery; an ordinary rerun fails immediately rather than completing or restoring the archive.
evidence: Current remediation_changelog_archive.py SHA-256 5a9addf675f3e33dcc2e4df39e303927be106b647a14f850df6d37f5baf86041 writes final paths at lines 360-368 and verifies only at line 369.

Temporary-root fault injection raised OSError on manifest write after both segment files and the compact source were written. The source contained the compact-index marker, two segment files existed, the manifest was absent, and a retry raised FileExistsError on the existing archive directory.
Current tests cover successful preservation/link verification and deliberate tampering only after a successful archive; they have no write-failure, verify-failure, rollback, or retry recovery case.
Structured all-worker deduplication found no existing segment_archive or remediation_changelog_archive root cause.
existing_safeguards: The tool refuses an already-existing archive directory, builds the full plan in memory, records hashes/counts/order in a manifest, and performs comprehensive post-write verification.
safeguard_gap: Those integrity checks detect a bad final state only after irreversible final-path writes and supply no automatic restoration or resumable recovery.
tests_missing: idempotent retry or resumable partial archive recovery
recommended_remediation: Write all segments and the manifest under a sibling temporary directory, verify them against the original source before publication, write the compact source to a temporary file, then atomically rename/replace final artifacts with a rollback journal. Preserve the original source bytes until every final rename succeeds and recognize/recover owned partial staging state.
remediation_risk: Medium: cross-file atomicity on Windows needs careful rename ordering and interruption tests; the original ledger must remain recoverable throughout.
validation_rung: Focused fault-injection tests for every publication step and verification failure, interruption/retry tests in temporary repositories, then canonical archive verification; representative real-media validation is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Related in atomicity impact to AUDIT-FIND-W11-015, but distinct: that finding concerns release-history overwrite/rollback, while this tool has no staging or rollback for remediation-ledger segmentation.
